messages.author: 048d1222bb0af667
messages.subject: Survival analysis with INLA
parts:
Hello, everyone

I'm now entering a new stage in my thesis project and I want to use the survival part of INLA.
I didn't find the papers about this topic in the website as told in the FAQ section so I was wondering if someone has access to them and could share them with me.

If not, I'm very interested in somo tutorials ou case studies to see concrete examples and also in the teoric part of the concepts use in the code so I know exactly what I'm doing.

I really appreciate any help!
Thank you a lot!
Ema Biscaia

messages.author: 334c7505e0b5cf65
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Survival analysis with INLA
parts:
Hi,

You can check some stuff here:

https://becarioprecario.bitbucket.io/inla-gitbook/ch-survival.html

But the INLA developers have produced some nice new features for joint models. Janet’s arXiv papers may be a good starting point: https://arxiv.org/search/stat?searchtype=author&query=van+Niekerk%2C+J

And also the list os papers in the R-INLA website:

https://www.r-inla.org/learnmore/papers

Best,

Virgilio

Hi, Virgilio

Thank you very much for your answer.
Yes, I have been following your book and it has helped me a lot.

However my data is not measure over time so it is not longitudinal. I just have an interval-censored response variable, 2 covariates, 1 random effect and a spatial component. In this case is joint modelling appropriate?

Thank you for your time!
Ema Biscaia
